title: Sacred Heart women's basketball begins road trip at Canisius
text:
Jessica Mannetti, Head Coach at Sacred Heart Pioneers Women's Basketball | https://sacredheartpioneers.com/
Jessica Mannetti, Head Coach at Sacred Heart Pioneers Women's Basketball | https://sacredheartpioneers.com/
The Sacred Heart Pioneers women's basketball team will begin a two-game trip in upstate New York with a matchup against the Canisius Golden Griffins on Thursday. The game, set for 6:30 p.m. at the Koessler Athletic Center in Buffalo, will be broadcast live on ESPN+.
Sacred Heart enters the contest with a 6-3 record in Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) play after completing their non-conference schedule at 2-7. Senior guard Amelia Wood has led the team, scoring double figures in 13 consecutive games and averaging 14.9 points per game this season. She is also second on the team in rebounding, averaging 6.3 per game, and leads in assists (39), steals (46), and blocks (14). Junior forward Nalyce Dudley follows with an average of 12.3 points per game and leads the team in shooting percentage at 47.7 percent overall, which increases to 54.2 percent inside the arc.
Freshman point guard Sophie Nascimento has contributed significantly during conference play, averaging nine points per MAAC game and twelve over her last five outings. As a team, Sacred Heart is shooting just under 40 percent from the field but has struggled with ball control, averaging nearly nineteen turnovers per game.
Canisius comes into Thursday's matchup with a 1-7 MAAC record after recently losing to Mount St. Mary's by seven points. The Golden Griffins have been outscored by an average of nearly sixteen points this season but are shooting forty-one percent from the field—third best in their league—and have made seventy-three three-pointers so far this year. Junior forward Shariah Gailes leads Canisius with averages of 14.3 points and 8.3 rebounds per game while shooting fifty-three percent from the floor.
The teams will meet for just the fourth time; Sacred Heart currently holds a two-to-one advantage after winning their most recent meeting less than three weeks ago.
Following Thursday’s contest, Sacred Heart will remain in upstate New York to face Niagara on Saturday afternoon as they aim for another season sweep after defeating Niagara earlier this month.
